identity.title: Enhancing Generative Auto-bidding with Offline Reward Evaluation and Policy Search

problem.claim: Improve offline auto-bidding beyond the exploration limits of static-data generative bidding.

gap.claim: Existing AIGB methods are bottlenecked by their inability to explore beyond the static offline dataset with feedback.

contributions.claim: AIGB-Pearl integrates generative planning with policy optimization through offline reward evaluation and policy search.
It uses a trajectory evaluator and a KL-Lipschitz-constrained score-maximization scheme described as provably sound for safe, efficient exploration beyond offline data.
It develops a practical synchronous-coupling algorithm to provide the regularity required by the proposed scheme.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present AIGB-Pearl as a novel integration of generative planning and policy optimization, with evaluator-guided constrained score maximization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance in extensive experiments on simulated and real-world advertising systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: Auto-bidding is framed as important for improving advertising performance.
AIGB is described as outperforming typical offline RL-based auto-bidding methods by learning a conditional generative planner from offline data.
The abstract identifies a performance bottleneck caused by AIGB's inability to explore beyond static data with feedback.
AIGB-Pearl adds trajectory evaluation, constrained score maximization, and synchronous coupling; the authors report state-of-the-art results in simulated and real-world systems.

source_observation.claim: The method links generated-score evaluation to a constrained optimization scheme intended to regulate exploration beyond offline data.

lessons.interpretation: This offers a concrete way to align a proposed capability with an explicit safety or regularity mechanism.
lessons.application: When presenting offline-to-online or out-of-distribution policy improvement, pair the exploration objective with a named evaluator and an explicit constraint or regularization condition.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when no meaningful evaluator or defensible constraint can be defined for the target domain.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, datasets, baselines beyond the general comparison, or ablations.
The conditions and scope of the claimed provable soundness and required model regularity are unspecified.
It is unclear how simulated and real-world systems differ or what 'state-of-the-art' comparison set was used.
